programme.title: Heart Surgeons Ep.1
programme.desc: The heart transplant operation of a famous politician is held at Taesan University Hospital. Park Tae Soo works on that operation together by Choi Seok Han's request, but he leaves the hospital with the donor's heart. Why did he leave with the heart? What happened to make this happen? Stay tuned to find out. Tae Soo's mother gets in a critical state, and Tae Soo becomes desperate to find a doctor who is willing to take her in. Tae Soo and Woo Jin frantically search for a hospital available, but they keep having difficulties. However, they finally reach Choi Seok Han by calling his number.

programme.title: Heart Surgeons Ep.2
programme.desc: Seok Han decides to do the surgery for Tae Soo's mom. Later, Tae Soo joins Taesan University Hospital as a fellow. However, he seems to be always cleaning up after Dong Joon's mess. As such days go by, Hee Dong suddenly orders Tae Soo to send a dying patient to another hospital. Tae Soo decides to do surgery for the patient he was ordered to send away. He manages to succeed with the help from Seok Han. Meanwhile, an emergency occurs during Soo Yeon's way back to Korea. Soo Yeon has no choice but to take the patient to the nearest hospital, but they don't have the equipment and supplies needed.

programme.title: Heart Surgeons Ep.3
programme.desc: Finding himself in a critical situation with no other viable option, Doctor Park Tae Soo convinces Doctor Yoon Soo Yeon to use super glue and a piece of a latex glove to patch a bleeding heart. Miraculously, the makeshift patch stops the bleeding, and the patient is rushed to Taesan University Hospital. Meanwhile, as Tae Soo prepares to go in for surgery, his mother calls to hear his voice. Tae Soo's mother goes into cardiac arrest. Luckily, Doctor Yoon Soo Yeon manages to get her on the ECMO machine and saves her life. With his mother in stable condition, Tae Soo meets with the family members of the patient who suffered the cardiac tamponade and decides to disclose that super glue was used to save his life. Right then, he sees who the uncle is and reconsiders telling the fact.

programme.title: Heart Surgeons Ep.4
programme.desc: Knowing her very existence could have been the reason for Professor Choi not being able to save his daughter's life, Soo Yeon visits Yoo Bin's memorial to show her respect. Tae Soo watches Professor Choi tormented by the memory of losing his daughter and walks away in sympathy. Despite his brother being alive, Hwang Jin Chul shows up to the hospital and threatens Tae Soo for using super glue. Taesan University Hospital director, Yoon Hyun Il, fires Tae Soo after he hears of his super glue procedure. However, his brother, Yoon Hyun Mook, the chief executive, hears about Hyun Il diverting funds from the Africa project and plans to have Hyun Il resign. Meanwhile, Soo Yeon sides with Tae Soo and tries to find a way to save his position at the hospital."

programme.title: Heart Surgeons Ep.5
programme.desc: Blackmailed, Professor Choi Seok Han faces a predicament that could lead him to find out the truth behind his daughter's death. The thought of never finding out what happened torments him and pushes him to the surgery room. Meanwhile, Tae Soo stands on guard and opposes the idea. Tae Soo's mother finally awakes from surgery but still urgently needs a heart transplant. Soo Yeon has difficulty breathing and plans to have surgery done by Professor Choi Seok Han. Meanwhile, Professor Choi Seok Han suffers from knowing the truth about his daughter's death and plans to get his revenge.

programme.title: Heart Surgeons Ep.6
programme.desc: Even with Hyun Il's confession and a plea for forgiveness, Hyun Mok stands firm on his decision to see him leave Taesan University Hospital. After meeting with Hyun Il, Hyun Mok and Soo Yeon get into an accident and are both seriously injured. When they arrive at the hospital, Hyun Mok begs Professor Choi to save Soo Yeon's life once again. The faculty attends Hyun Mok's funeral and starts to gossip. Everyone knows with Hyun Mok dead and Soo Yeon grasping onto her life, Hyun Il will become the hospital's chief director. programme.desc: Sausages are coated in a rice batter, instead of a flour batter, and fried to make a delicious and healthy snack. Korean-style sweet pancakes with sweet and nutting fillings are another winter delicacy. Try these popular snack recipes for a tasty winter break!

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Braised beef short ribs are a staple for special occasions, including holiday and birthday meals. Beef short ribs are seasoned in sweet soy sauce and braised until tender. Another popular holiday dish is glass noodles stir-fried with a variety of vegetables. What better way to spend this Seol, or Lunar New Year's Day, than to make a hearty meal using these two recipes?

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Dried pollock fish, bean curd and bean sprouts are simmered in a rich stock to make a hangover soup great for breakfast. After indulging in this tasty and filling soup, try a deep fried spiral-cut whole potato on a skewer. These two delicacies will keep you fueled for the rest of your trip.

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Looking for quick and delicious lunch box recipes for work? Spicy stir-fried pork with kimchi and vegetables makes a filling and tasty side dish to rice. Pack it with potatoes braised in a soy sauce-based glaze for an extra layer of flavor. Check out these recipes and fuel your workday!

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Kimchi and ham fried rice is a quick and easy lunch option for work. A side dish that works well alongside the fried rice is a crunchy cucumber salad tossed in a sweet and spicy sauce. Follow these recipes for a nutritious and convenient office lunch.

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Gimbap is a staple in lunch boxes, but making traditional gimbap rolls can be a hassle. There is an easier and quicker way to make this healthy and delicious dish. Fold the ingredients inside the laver into a square shape instead of rolling it. Pack it with spicy fish cake stir-fry, another popular lunch box recipe.

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Looking for recipes to brighten your spring table? Webfoot octopuses are known to taste best and be extra nutritional during their breeding season from March to May. Stir-fry them in a spicy sauce to make a wonderful seasonal dish. The perfect dish to pair with it is a green laver and Korean radish salad tossed in a sweet and sour brine.

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: On this Chuseok special, Chef Ryan shares with us how to make kkochijeon, or Korean pan-fried skewers. Meat and vegetables are threaded onto skewers, dipped in flour and beaten egg and pan-fried to make this colorful dish. Check out this quick and fun recipe to make as a family this holiday.

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Blood sausage is one of the most beloved foods in Korea. The chewy sausage is stir-fried with spicy sauce to make sundae bokkeum, a popular late-night snack. Try it with sweet and savory corn cheese which cuts the spiciness of the stir-fry. Both are as tasty as they are easy to make, when you are looking to much on something late at night.

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Looking for recipes that will bring back your lost appetite this spring? A bowl of noodle soup made of fresh littleneck clams at their plumpest has a refreshing broth and a savory taste that will leave you want for more. Pair with briny seaweed pancakes with a crispy outside and a chewy inside.

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Chef Ryan shares with us how to make myeolchi bokkeum, or stir-fried anchovies, which is a staple dish in Korean households. It is made by stir-frying small dried anchovies with assorted nuts and coating them in a sweet and savory glaze. Perfect as a side dish or snack, these crispy anchovies are sure to have you finishing a bowl of rice in no time.

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Chef Ryan shares with us how to make gochu twigim, or fried stuffed peppers, one of the most popular street foods in Korea. Chili peppers are stuffed with a mixture of pork and vegetables and deep-fried, resulting in a dish that is juicy inside and crispy outside. The chef will show the original version featuring Korean chili peppers, as well as a creative version with Jalapeño peppers.

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Chef Ryan shares with us how to make ganjang saewu, or soy sauce marinated shrimp. This popular Korean pickled seafood offers a subtly sweet and savory taste that delights the palate. The secret lies in the special marinade made from soy sauce and a mix of vegetables. Impress your loved ones with this delicious seafood recipe.

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Chef Ryan shares with us how to make dakgalbi, or spicy stir-friend chicken, which is one of the most popular dishes among international travelers visiting Korea. It is made by stir-frying marinated chicken in a red chili paste-based sauce with sweet potatoes, cabbage and cheese. Learn how to make this delicious blend of spicy, sweet and savory.

programme.title: 1DAY 1KOREA
programme.desc: Chef Ryan shares with us how to make red radish kimchi, a twist on the traditional Korean yeolmu (young radish) kimchi with a more readily available ingredient – radish. Join us to learn more about this unique recipe for refreshing fusion kimchi with a crisp and crunchy texture.

programme.title: Dunedin, St. Peter-Clearwater
programme.desc: In this season opener, the hosts explore Dunedin Golf Club, a beautifully restored Donald Ross-designed course in Florida. They highlight its challenging holes, firm greens, and historical significance, while showcasing the area's variety of public and private courses. Off the course, the episode dives into local activities like paddleboarding, beach running, and fishing, emphasizing the unique artsy vibe of St. Pete versus the lively, event-filled atmosphere of Clearwater. The hosts share playful on-course banter, bets, and golf tips, wrapping up with thanks to local sponsors, Visit St. Pete-Clearwater, and the Fenway Hotel for making the visit special.

programme.title: The Swing Clinic: Firestone 1 of 2
programme.desc: In this episode of The Swing Clinic, Jimmy Hanlin visits the Kaulig Championship at Firestone Country Club in Akron, Ohio. He sits down with Kaulig Companies Executive Chairman Matt Kaulig to discuss his ties to the event and community. On the course, Hanlin works with Kaulig Racing's AJ Allmendinger, Ty Dillon, and Daniel Dye, offering practical swing tips with plenty of laughs. PGA Tour pro Dicky Pride also joins to share driver distance techniques, focusing on patience and smooth transitions. Mixing celebrity golf, instruction, and local flavor, the show captures the excitement of a major tournament week.

programme.title: Vinoy, St. Pete-Clearwater
programme.desc: Jimmy Hanlin and Natalie Gulbis tee it up at the scenic Vinoy Golf Club in St. Petersburg, Florida, showcasing a course that blends history, beauty, and playability. The front nine features wide fairways and accessible greens—perfect for birdie opportunities—while the back nine tightens up with tougher green complexes and strategic challenges. The episode mixes light competition, golf instruction, and local flavor. Between shots, Jimmy and Natalie explore the luxurious Vinoy Resort, sample the signature “1925” tequila cocktail, and take in the vibrant, active vibe of the St. Pete-Clearwater area, from waterfront views to bustling beach scenes.

programme.title: MeatEater
programme.sub-title: Montana Muzzleloader Hunting for Mule Deer
programme.desc: Steven Rinella takes on Montana's week-long big game heritage season with a traditional muzzleloader. With flintlock in hand, Steve's after mule deer in a desolate and broken sage brush landscape. After a long few months of evading hunters, these deer have perfected how to stay alive. But stalking a deer into range isn't the only hurdle to navigate.

programme.title: MeatEater

programme.title: MeatEater
programme.desc: Steven Rinella travels to Tanzania for his first African safari with professional hunter, Morgan Potter. In this episode, Morgan and his team show Steve the ropes of hunting in this foreign terrain for otherworldly big game species. Steve's quest for a cape buffalo moves to the side burner when the team discovers an impressive roan antelope.

programme.title: MeatEater
programme.sub-title: Into the Clouds: Sitka Blacktail Deer
programme.desc: Steven Rinella charters a float plane to drop off on a remote lake in Alaska's coastal rainforest for a solo Sitka blacktail deer hunt. With challenging terrain, thick fog, and incessant rain, finding a buck won't be easy. But if Steve connects on a Sitka blacktail, he'll celebrate with a camp meal of rock-pounded tenderloin.

programme.title: MeatEater
programme.sub-title: The Sweetest Meat: Alaskan Black Bear
programme.desc: As summer turns to fall, Steve heads into the backcountry of Alaska's Chugach Range. The bears here are on a quest to fatten up on high elevation blueberries before they hibernate for the winter. Steve will need to hike into steep, rugged terrain to find a fat black bear and some of the finest tasting meat available to the American hunter.

programme.title: Cal in the Field
programme.desc: Cal heads to a waterfowl mecca — California's Sacramento Valley — where he joins Sean Doherty and local guide Scott Feist for a hunt in the heart of the nation's largest agricultural region. The rice fields they're hunting provide vital habitat for waterfowl outside of planting season. Thanks to ongoing conservation efforts, native ducks, geese, and shorebirds have returned to the area. The same water that grows food and attracts birds could also help revive the native fishery.

programme.title: Das Boat
programme.sub-title: Steven Rinella and Grant Gulley Troll for Lake Trout on Lake Michigan
programme.desc: Steve introduces you to Dos Boat. Steve gets to South Haven, MI, where he recruits the help of local charter captain Grant Gully. Steve, Grant, and a fabricator put in 10 hours of work getting the boat ready to fish for lake trout in 100 feet of water. Grant is somewhat skeptical boat‚ ability to handle the water of Lake Michigan. They discuss Jon Gary îSteve‚ fishing mentor and the original captain of Dos Boat‚ the young anglers Jon influenced, the decline (and comeback) of the lake trout.

programme.title: Das Boat
programme.sub-title: Au Sable River Trout with Janis Putelis and Brian Kozminski
programme.desc: Steve hauls Dos Boat to Boyne City, Michigan. Janis Putelis connects with trout fishing guide Brian Kozminski. They try to get the boat prepared for a nighttime river expedition by setting it up for rowing. Along the way they discuss: the history and fish of the Iconic Au Sable river, the giant hexagenia mayflies that hatch there, whether or not fish give a damn how pretty your cast is, the load of fishing options in Michigan, and the ability to pivot when conditions suck.

programme.title: Das Boat
programme.sub-title: Menominee River Smallmouth with Joe Cermele and Tim Landwehr
programme.desc: Dos Boat crosses the Straits of Mackinaw and heads west to the Wisconsin, U.P. border. Joe Cermele teams up Tim Landwehr. They burn Tim‚ home river on a fishing show. A proposed sulfide mine threatens the future of this fishery, and he wants you to know about it. Other topics discussed: finding big fish in skinny water, how delicious northern pike are, losing a bass but catching the ‚ follower, and a hell of a lot more.

programme.title: Das Boat
programme.sub-title: Northern Wisconsin Musky with Oliver Ngy and Kevin Harlander
programme.desc: Dos Boat meets up with Oliver Ngy and Kevin Harlander in North Central Wisconsin. Oliver and Kevin are here for two things: big musky and delicious panfish. They give Das Boat a lake fishing upgrade with electronics and a powerful trolling motor. They convert a cooler into a livewell to keep bait and fish alive. They discuss whether or not it really takes 10,000 casts to catch a musky, losing the fish of a lifetime right at the boat, the figure 8, how bluegills make you feel like a winner.

programme.title: Das Boat
programme.sub-title: Big Mouth Buffalo with Ryan Callaghan and Miles Nolte
programme.desc: Ryan Callaghan and Miles Nolte travel to Minnesota to try to catch big mouth buffalo. The guys build a raised casting platform on Das Boat. They meet Alec Lackmann, the world‚ foremost expert on big mouth buffalo. Cal and Miles tag along with Alec to help release some buffalo that he was studying. Cal and Miles head over to the Mississippi River to try their luck on a population of river buffalo that don't get hunted with bows.

programme.title: Landry: Hair Chronicles
programme.desc: Landry's energy is contagious. Coming to the Dry Bar stage with a fresh, bold take on common tropes, he describes the difference between first-class passengers and everyone else a DUI and an IUD and Cracker Barrel versus any yard sale.

programme.title: Andrew Hobbs
programme.desc: Have you ever, as an adult, been bullied by a healthcare professional or popular middle school girl? Andrew has. The comedy of Andrew Hobbs encapsulates the bizarre awkwardness of belated maturity and his attempts to appear in control. Andrew will have you rolling with laughter as he twists a narrative of humor and heart from his own life experiences and observations. His comedy has been featured in comedy festivals across the country. He has been perfecting his craft since childhood and throughout adulthood.

programme.title: Corey Rodrigues
programme.desc: Corey is a highly sought after national touring college, club and corporate and cruise ship performer. He was the winner of The Catch a New Rising Star, The Funniest Comic in New England and the 2017 Big Sky Comedy Festivals. Rodrigues has been featured on the hilarious Gotham Live, Laughs on Fox and True Tv's Laff Mobbs Laff Tracks television shows and currently can be heard on Sirius XM. He combines comedy from his own life and the lives of those around him. Mix that with a hilarious point of view and he's able to talk about just about anything.

programme.title: Costaki Economopoulos
programme.desc: For 20 years Costaki has been living his dream as a full-time stand up comic. He has written jokes for Bette Midler, Jay Leno, MTV, and BET. You may have seen him on Showtime or heard him on Sirius, but you probably know him best from his regular appearances on the nationally syndicated Bob & Tom Radio Show.

programme.title: Karen Rontowski
programme.desc: Karen Rontowski's fast-paced, quirky and charmingly optimistic comedy has been featured in clubs, TV, radio, and at corporate events all around the world. Her stand- up showcases endearing, self-effacing and intelligent characters that catch you by surprise every time. Karen uniquely blends comedy with her experience as a Paranormal Investigator and Reiki master. From fun with her family to her travels all over this great country Karen has fun where ever she goes. Her lighthearted confusion entertains kids of all ages. She is fascinated with the “afterlife” is convinced she will someday have a near death experience because, “I never finish anything.” She explains, “Sometimes a ghost will just do the same thing over and over in life. That's why I want to move into a house that is haunted by a maid." Karen's comedy is now featured in the new line of greeting cards called “Frank and Funny” sold at Target stores everywhere and is the comedy writer for “Haunted Magazine.” She is a regular on the Bob and Tom Radio Show and is a featured performer on their CD. Karen has appeared on The Late Show with David Letterman, Sirius Satellite Radio, Comics Unleashed, Comedy.com, Live at Gotham and Comedy Central. She has opened for show biz legends including Bob Hope, Ray Charles, David Brenner and the Monkees.

programme.title: Heather Mabbott: I Didn't Mean To Say That
programme.desc: Her quick wit and unique style has dazzled audiences all over the country. Heather is a clean comedian and has performed with some of the best, like Caroline Rhea, Jimmy Walker, Bobcat Goldthwait, Bruce Baum, Sinbad, and many, many more.

programme.title: Jordan Makin
programme.desc: Born and raised in the heart of Utah County, Jordan Makin had to compensate for his red hair and uneventful childhood by learning to be funny. His unique observations will make you laugh and his stories about feeling awkward will help you appreciate your life more. He has worked with many comedy greats, such as Marc Maron, Ryan Hamilton, and Drew Lynch. His comedy has been featured at the Finger Lakes Comedy Festival and the Idaho Laugh Fest. Jordan is the co-creator and co-host of The Happy Valley Podcast.

programme.title: Helene Angley: Queen Size
programme.desc: Helene brings honesty to the stage that helps everyone relax-- and laugh at the joys and pains of aging, being a married mother of two and all that the generation gap brings!

programme.title: Fred Klett
programme.desc: Fred Klett has built a career from being a clean comedian, a style that is his trademark. His comedy is G-rated and focused to appeal to families with members of all ages since much of his material is taken from his experiences growing up in a large Christian family. As a mainstream performer, his brand of humor is rare and refreshing and is rooted in his faith in Christ and belief in the Holy Scriptures.

programme.title: James Johann
programme.desc: James' childhood upbringing was significantly influenced by country music, countless bad hair cuts, and Catholic school. In 1991, James began his stand-up career in Kansas City. Today, James is a long-time veteran of the stand-up comedy circuit, performing at clubs across the country. His self-deprecating sense of humor and high energy style come together to create a unique onstage persona. James relies more on his brain than the profane and his comedy is a truthful and hilarious reflection of life as he sees it.

It's a simple, sweet rhyme about the magic of making wishes on falling stars. She tries a few different rhymes as she goes, noting them on her paper. She is startled to hear applause from Mr. Longface Caterpillar who has heard her recital.

It's her tenth attempt to create the world's first Rainbow Smoothie! She has even painted one wall of her café rainbow colors in honor of the soon-to-be new item on the menu. No one dares breathe for fear of spoiling the delicate touch of a master smoothie-squirter at work.

programme.title: Tarzan and Jane
programme.desc: Baby Tarzan is rescued from a plane crash by the gorilla, Kala, and brought to a Shaman who treats Tarzan's injuries with a mix of native medicines and experimental science - saving Tarzan's life and giving him supernatural animal powers in the process. Tarzan is returned to Kala and remains in the jungle, defending animals from poachers, hunters and other threats. As a teenager, Tarzan is discovered by an expedition team from London, paid for by his billionaire grandfather. It is during this expedition where Tarzan meets Jane, and they become fast friends. Later, a series of mishaps takes him to London, reuniting Tarzan not only with his long lost family, but Jane as well. It is here where Tarzan and Jane learn to navigate the “urban jungle” of London, and uncover a dastardly plot to steal and sell exotic animals to the highest bidder! It is up to our heroes to figure out who is behind this sinister deed, and return the animals to their rightful homes in the jungle.

programme.title: JUNGWOO 'SUGAR' MV
programme.desc: NCT JUNGWOO's first solo single “SUGAR” is a groovy pop song with swing‑infused drums, a witty bassline, and a smooth, catchy melody. The lyrics send a warm message of gratitude to fans, wishing that past memories and future moments are all sweet. The music video brings this sweetness to life with colorful, sugar-inspired visuals, while the performance highlights JUNGWOO's stylish movements and precise choreography, showcasing his unique stage presence.

programme.title: TAEYEON 'Panorama' MV
programme.desc: TAEYEON celebrates the 10th anniversary of her solo debut with the compilation album Panorama, featuring the Pop Rock title track “인사 (Panorama).” The song pairs vibrant piano, synths, and a strong drum line with soaring guitar riffs and TAEYEON's delicate yet powerful vocals. The music video presents a cinematic story of TAEYEON, who has lost her memory, and a girl who helps restore it — a metaphor for the bond between the artist and her fans, SONEs. Its emotional, road-movie-style visuals reveal SONEs as the hidden protagonist. The 24-track album offers a retrospective of her past decade, unfolding like a panorama of her solo journey.

programme.title: WayV '白色定格 (Eternal White)' MV
programme.desc: The title track “白色定格 (Eternal White)” is a dance-pop song that blends a rhythmic saxophone riff with energetic drum beats, creating a warm atmosphere through the harmony of powerful rap and sweet vocals. The lyrics express a strong determination to break free from time frozen like a white winter and to keep moving forward, capturing the hearts of listeners..

programme.title: DOYOUNG 'Promise' MV
programme.desc: The lyrics, written by DOYOUNG, capture the feelings he couldn't easily express as his love grew deeper. Even if the confession comes late, it delivers a sincerity and emotional resonance stronger than any other words.The title track “Promise” is an impressive ballad that begins with a minimal piano melody and gradually builds emotional depth as strings are added in the latter half.

programme.title: DOYOUNG 'Whistle (Feat. BELLE of KISS OF LIFE)' Live Clip
programme.desc: Layered over a jazz guitar melody, the sweet vocals blend together like a conversation, conveying a lovely sense of fluttering excitement. The track “Whistle (Feat. BELLE of KISS OF LIFE)” is an R&B ballad that depicts a moment of exchanging feelings through the sound of a whistle. With Belle participating as a featuring artist and harmonizing with DOYOUNG, the synergy between the two elevates the charm of the song even further.

programme.title: EXO 'REVERXE' Trailer
programme.desc: At the end of the trailer, the title of EXO's 8th full-length album, “REVERXE,” was finally revealed. Based on EXO's universe storyline — “the day we truly become one, a new world will open” — the album name reinterprets the word “Reverse” in EXO's own style, carrying the meaning “a new world opens once again,” further heightening anticipation.EXO has returned with a new trailer.

programme.title: EXO 'I'm Home' MV
programme.desc: EXO has hinted at a new winter song that follows the emotional resonance of the chart resurgence of “First Snow.” “I'm Home” is a pop ballad that blends delicate piano melodies with lush strings, expressing the happiness of being reunited with loved ones and the wish to stay in this moment for a long time.

programme.title: Eliane Elias
programme.desc: There's no question about it: with a Grammy for Best Latin Jazz Album for her recording ‘Made In Brazil', seven previous Grammy nominations, four ‘Gold Disc Awards', and three ‘Best Vocal Album Awards' in Japan, Eliane Elias has taken her place in the pantheon of music giants. In her projects, Elias wears many hats: she serves as producer, composer, lyricist, arranger, pianist, and vocalist. In this concert broadcast, recorded live at the Philharmonie in Munich, Elias shows her distinctive and immediately recognizable musical style, which blends her Brazilian samba roots and her sensuous, alluring voice with her impressive instrumental bebop, jazz, classical, and compositional skills. She is an artist beyond category, and in this concert she performs with Jay Randall Anderson (bass) and Adam Nussbaum (drums).

programme.title: Dizzy Gillespie, Tony Coe, Derek Humble & Billy Mitchell
programme.desc: American jazz trumpeter, composer, and bandleader Dizzy Gillespie (1917-1993) was one of the seminal figures of the bebop movement. He fuses all musical forms rooted in African culture, such as music from Cuba, Latin America and the Caribbean, into his music. On November 4, 1970 he played a concert in Denmark with the Kenny Clarke/Francy Boland Big Band, performing Con Alma, Brother K, Now Hear My Meanin', Manteca, Let Me Outta Here, and Things Are Here.

programme.title: Gonzalo Rubalcaba, Ron Carter & Jul Barretto
programme.desc: 'Münchner Klaviersommer' was an annual concerts series that took place from 1981 to 1998 in Munich, Germany. Although the festival's name suggests a strong focus on piano music, it featured countless famous musicians from jazz and classical music – not just pianists. The concerts were usually held in July at The Gasteig, home of the Munich Philharmonic. In 1994, Cuban pianist Gonzalo Rubalcaba was one of the artists appearing here. With bassist Ron Carter - one of the living legends on this instrument - and highly talented Cuban jazz drummer Julio Barreto, Rubalcaba's trio marks an important step in the development of jazz trio playing in the 1990s. Moreover, it demonstrates the brilliant improvisational and technical abilities of Gonzalo Rubalcaba, who has become one of our present-day jazz legends.

programme.title: Wes Montgomery
programme.desc: An extraordinary collection of clips in all jazz genres from the most beautiful concerts and the most special festivals, performed by the finest jazz musicians.

programme.title: John Coltrane
programme.desc: Explore the music of one of the most influential and innovative saxophonists in jazz history: John Coltrane! Immerse yourself in this collection of remarkable performances from the early 1960s that showcase Coltrane's unparalleled artistry and unique sound during a transformative period in the artist's career. Recorded in various European cities, Coltrane is seen playing the songs “Autumn Leaves”, “Hackensack”, “My Favorite Things”, “I Want To Talk About You”, “Vigil”, and “Naima”. Tune in and experience why the music of John Coltrane has touched the lives of so many!

programme.title: Tigran Hamasyan & Mathias Eick
programme.sub-title: Tigran Hamasyan & Mathias Eick - November Music
programme.desc: November Music, a Dutch music festival in 's-Hertogenbosch, showcases today's prominent composers. It programs top-notch ensembles, jazz and world music pioneers, interdisciplinary concerts, and sound art. In 2019, Tigran Hamasyan and Mathias Eick played a duo performance here. Armenian pianist Hamasyan has claimed a category of his own in contemporary jazz. Norwegian trumpeter Mathias Eick is an undisputed master of his instrument.

programme.title: Paul Desmond
programme.desc: An extraordinary collection of clips in all jazz genres from the most beautiful concerts and the most special festivals, performed by the finest jazz musicians.

programme.title: Baden Powell, Ernesto Ribeiro-Goncalves, Helio Schiavo & Alfredo Bessa
programme.desc: Recorded in 1971 in Paris, France, Brazilian, classically trained bossa nova guitarist Baden Powell and his quartet play Pai, Lotus (written by Baden Powell), Tristeza (by Haroldo Lobo/Niltinho), Round Midnight (by Thelonious Monk), Nega do cabelo duro (by David Nasser/Rubens Soares), and Aos pes da cruz (by Zé da Zilda/Marino Pinto). Powell is joined by Ernesto Ribeiro-Gonçalves on double bass, Helio Schiavo on drums, and Alfredo Bessa on percussion.

programme.title: Christian McBride
programme.desc: On July 20, 2018, double bassist Christian McBride presented his band ‘New Jawn' at the Malta Jazz Festival. A five-time Grammy winner, McBride is one of the most requested, most recorded, and most respected figures in the music world today. Hailing from Philadelphia, this music luminary combines jazz, R&B, pop/rock, hip hop/neo-soul, and classical. Gracing the Malta Jazz stage with him are Nasheet Waits (drums), Marcus Strickland (tenor sax), and Josh Evans (trumpet).

programme.title: Arturo Sandoval
programme.desc: The North Sea Jazz Festival is the largest indoor music festival in the world, known globally as the event where the past, present and future of jazz are featured within three days. Next to a firm base of jazz as the festival's staple music genre, many others, such as blues, soul, funk, or hip hop, pass by. In 1986, Cuban trumpeter Arturo Sandoval brought his band with him to the North Sea Jazz Festival in The Hague. Featuring talented performers like pianist Hilario Durán and guitarist Jorge Chicoy, they displayed a master class in Latin jazz fusion.

programme.title: Mikhail Pletnev, Russian National Orchestra & Lucas Debargue
programme.sub-title: Pletnev conducts Bizet & Ravel's Concerto No. 1
programme.desc: Mikhail Pletnev leads the Russian National Orchestra (RNO) in a performance of Maurice Ravel's Piano Concerto No. 1 with Lucas Debargue as the soloist. The concert opens with a selection of music by Georges Bizet based on Alphonse Daudet's play 'L'Arlésienne'. The music is compiled by Mikhail Pletnev. The first movement of Ravel's Piano Concerto No. 1 contains five distinctive themes, of which three are reminiscent of jazz. Debargue's performance of Ravel's concerto is followed by Gabriel Fauré's Barcarolle No. 4. The performance was recorded at Tchaikovsky Concert Hall in Moscow as part of the Ninth RNO Grand Festival.

programme.title: David Grimal & Les Dissonances
programme.sub-title: Beethoven - Symphony No. 4 in B-flat major, Op. 60
programme.desc: Les Dissonances is a collective of artists founded by violinist David Grimal in 2004. The conductorless ensemble consists of musicians from the most prestigious European orchestras, international soloists, and young talents. In this performance, Les Dissonances perform Ludwig van Beethoven's Symphony No. 4 in B-flat major, Op. 60. Count Franz von Oppersdorff, who adored Beethoven's Symphony No. 2, offered the composer a large sum to write a similar work. Completed in the autumn of 1806, the symphony's first performance was at a private concert in Vienna in March of 1807. Symphony No. 4 is often overshadowed by its revolutionary predecessor and successor. With its lightweight and cheerful nature, Symphony No. 4 contrasts with the two aforementioned works. This performance was recorded at Opéra de Dijon, France, in 2013.

programme.title: The Philharmonics
programme.desc: Cinematic classical clips and energizing concert pieces featuring up-and-coming artists.

programme.title: Andrea Bacchetti
programme.desc: At the age of eleven, Italian pianist Andrea Bacchetti (*1977) debuted with Italian chamber orchestra I Solisti Veneti under the baton of Claudio Scimone. He performed on international festivals and in prestigious concert halls worldwide. Besides, he appeared with several renowned orchestras such as Lucerne Festival Strings, Camerata Salzburg, and Prague Chamber Orchestra. In the current recital, Bacchetti performs J. S. Bach's celebrated Goldberg Variations, BWV 988. Completed in 1741, the work is named after German harpsichordist Johann Gottlieb Goldberg, who might have been the first to have performed the work. Bach's masterpiece consists of an aria and a set of thirty variations. Rather than writing variations on the aria's melody, Bach used the accompanying bass line as his starting point. This performance was recorded at Theater Carlo Felice in Genoa, Italy, on April 13, 2015.

programme.title: David Grimal & Les Dissonances
programme.desc: Les Dissonances is a collective of artists founded by violinist David Grimal in 2004. The conductorless ensemble consists of musicians from the most prestigious European orchestras, international soloists, and young talents. In this performance, Les Dissonances perform Johannes Brahms' String Sextet No. 1 in B-flat major, Op. 18. The work is scored for two violins, two violas, and two cellos. Brahms wrote his only two string sextets at the very beginning of his career. String Sextet No. 1 was written in 1860. Brahms was one of the first to compose for this ensemble, blazing a trail for Antonín Dvořák, Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, Arnold Schoenberg, and others. This performance was recorded at Opéra de Dijon, France, in 2013.

programme.title: Freiburger Barockorchester, German Brass, Barbara Bonney & Matthias Goerne
programme.desc: This splendid Christmas concert was recorded live from the Freiburg Cathedral in 1999. It features soprano Barbara Bonney, recognized worldwide for the clarity of her voice and the precision of her diction, and the baritone Matthias Goerne, one of the most promising singers of his generation. Accompanied by the Baroque Orchestra of Freiburg and the German Brass, they perform pieces from Bach's Christmas Oratorio (BWV 248), Mozart's Mass in C minor (KV 427), and Handel's Messiah.

programme.title: Sir Simon Rattle & London Symphony Orchestra
programme.desc: Sir Simon Rattle conducts the London Symphony Orchestra (LSO) in Antonín Dvořák's spirited Slavonic Dances, Op. 46 (Nos. 1-8). These 16 folk dances earned Dvořák, who was a relative newcomer when he wrote them, great success. Originally composed for piano four hands, the London Symphony Orchestra plays the orchestral version of these brilliant works. This performance was recorded at LSO St. Luke's on Old Street in London, UK, on September 23, 2020.

programme.title: Coro Infantil Da Universidade de Lisboa, Orquesta Gulbenkian, Coro Gulbenkian & Michel Corboz
programme.desc: Bach's famous Saint Matthew Passion premiered on Good Friday of 1727 in the St. Thomas Church of Leipzig in Eastern Germany. Since then, it has become essential to the repertoire of Easter compositions. In this 2014 concert from the Grande Auditório Gulbenkian in Lisbon, the Portuguese Gulbenkian Orchestra interprets the work under the baton of Swiss conductor Michel Corboz, accompanied by the wonderful vocalists of the Gulbenkian Choir, and the children's choir Coro Infantil da Universidade de Lisboa. The soloists are Sandrine Piau (soprano), Carlos Mena (counter-tenor), Vincent Lièvre-Picard (evangelist), Christophe Genz (tenor), André Baleiro (Christ) and Peter Harvey (bass).

programme.title: Paul Simon
programme.desc: During the first leg of Paul Simon's triumphant, 2011 U.S. tour, he thrilled hometown fans with a special club performance at New York City's historic Webster Hall. The show presents this iconic artist working at the peak of his artistic and creative powers in an unusually intimate setting. The 20-song, 90-minute set list was drawn from his legendary career and includes several songs that haven't been performed live in many years. "Kodachrome," "Mother and Child Reunion," "Gone At Last" and "The Obvious Child" are just some of the highlights as well as songs from Simon's most recent album, 2011's So Beautiful or So What (Hear Music/Concord Music Group) including "Dazzling Blue," "Rewrite," "The Afterlife" and the album's propulsive title track.
